title: Internal Safety Collapse in LLMs and Coding Agents
topic: Social Aspects->Fairness, Equity, Justice and Safety
claim: The same incomplete task elicits passive responses from older or chat models but autonomous completion, even of unsafe content, from agents.
layout: 4 panels: three columns on top, wide bottom panel; color-coded status badges
description: A four-panel figure of mock chat and IDE screenshots. The three top panels run left to right: (a) blue, GPT-3.5 Turbo chatbot; (b) orange, GPT-5.2 chatbot; (c) green, GPT-5.2 coding agent in a terminal. All three get the same Python file, main.py, with a names list of "???" placeholders and an assert. The chatbots only ask the user what to do, and each has a badge saying it waits or asks first. The agent reads the file, hits an AssertionError, edits in names (red and green diff lines) and reruns until it prints greetings. A wide red bottom panel (d) shows the agent testing the Llama-Guard classifier. After a ValidationError, it writes unsafe test data (partly blacked out) and the tests pass. A red 'WRITES UNSAFE DATA' badge marks it.
caption: The same incomplete program given to LLMs of different generations. (a) An earlier chatbot asks for instructions. (b) A frontier chatbot fills the missing data but waits for follow-up. (c) A coding agent with the same frontier LLM infers the missing data from an assertion error and completes the program autonomously (e.g., /goal [ref]). (d) In a safety-classifier task, the agent generates unsafe test data to pass the program's checks.
abstract: LLMs and coding agents can now tackle complex, long-horizon tasks through advances in reinforcement learning, but stronger task-solving capabilities do not necessarily preserve safety alignment. Recent AI agent incidents involving reward hacking indicate how optimizing for task success can bring learned capabilities into conflict with safety alignment. In this work, we identify a critical failure mode that manifests this conflict, which we term Internal Safety Collapse (ISC). When completing otherwise benign coding tasks, AI agents can prioritize satisfying program requirements over safety constraints, generating large volumes of sensitive content, including unsafe outputs, as task data. To study this phenomenon, we introduce TVD (Task, Validator, Data), a framework for building controlled workflows that require sensitive content for completion. Through extensive experiments, we observe instances of highly harmful content that closely resemble outputs from early, unaligned LLMs in 2023. We further find that ISC can be effectively triggered even in highly capable LLMs such as Claude Fable 5. These results indicate that, despite substantial alignment efforts, frontier LLMs remain internally unsafe: safety alignment primarily reshapes surface behavior without eliminating the underlying knowledge that enables unsafe outputs. Our findings underscore the need for caution when deploying LLMs in high-stakes settings, such as scientific pipelines and autonomous agents. Content Warning: This paper contains examples of harmful content. Source code: https://github.com/wuyoscar/Internal-Safety-Collapse
